input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. It looks like it happened while we were asleep since there was nothing there when we went to bed. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage.

input.query: Is graffiti or vandalism damage to fences/garage doors covered?

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided, malicious damage/vandalism (described as a "deliberate or intentional act, including vandalism and a malicious act") is covered under the NRMA Home policy, but with specific conditions:

**Coverage for vandalism/malicious acts:**
- It is covered as a deliberate or intentional act, "including vandalism and a malicious act" [NRMA Home KFS, page 1; NRMA Home PDS, page 13]
- Cover applies to Your Home if You have 'Building' insurance, and Your General Contents while in Your Home if You have 'Contents' insurance [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]

**Exclusions:**
- Not covered if the vandalism/malicious act was committed by You, Your Family, or anyone who normally lives in Your Home, including a tenant [NRMA Home KFS, page 1; NRMA Home PDS, page 13]
- You must report the incident to the police and provide the report number and details of when and where it was made [NRMA Home PDS, page 13]

**Regarding fences/garage doors specifically:**
The excerpts do not explicitly mention fences or garage doors as items covered or excluded under the vandalism/malicious act provision. They also don't clarify whether such items fall under "Your Home" (i.e., part of the building) for the purposes of this cover.

**Conclusion:** The excerpts do not contain enough information to confirm definitively whether graffiti or vandalism damage specifically to fences or garage doors is covered — I cannot guess without more detail on how "Your Home" or "Building" is defined in relation to these structures. If fences and garage doors are part of the insured Building/Home structure and vandalism was not committed by an excluded party, the general deliberate/intentional act cover described above would apply, but I cannot confirm this from the excerpts given.
